reuse.why: The link rules go into two shared guards (ensureTargetAccountIsOpen, ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked) called by every provider, but Fintegra linking, its download, its balance computation and the takeover unlink are written as copies instead of reusing existing flows (unlinkAccount, the Akahu/SimpleFin link and download).

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount copies the whole link boilerplate, downloadFintegraTransactions and the processBankSyncDownload 'fintegra' branch copy the Akahu ones verbatim, and the replace path copies unlinkAccount's field-clearing update.

placement.why: Guards, link handler, download, server URL and types sit in the files where the other providers' equivalents live.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: The guard helpers are clean and consistently called, but ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked silently mutates another account when a flag is set (its name says it only checks), and Fintegra adds a sixth hand-maintained copy of the link/download/balance code.

bypasses_abstraction.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked in accounts/app.ts re-implements the local part of unlinkAccount (null-out of account_id, bank, balances, sync source, status) instead of sharing it.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra link/download/balance branch, unlink fields) are open copies of existing code, not renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked (created for step 1) gains a `replaceExistingLink` parameter and an `existing && replaceExistingLink` branch that turns the check into an unlink; all six link functions call both guards, none bypasses them.
